faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.intro: Short, honest answers about how the unlock card works, what is actually checked, and what we store.
faq.helpBody: Send us the short link or the step you are stuck on and we will take a look.
faq.content:
### What is Link Unlocker?
Link Unlocker turns a link or file into a short unlock page. You choose actions from the catalog and the content is revealed after the configured requirements are met. Some social steps require an authenticated account check; others complete with one click without verifying the platform action. A completed unlock is not a guarantee of new followers.

### Is Link Unlocker really free?
Yes. Creating links, protecting files, collecting email addresses, the bio page and the analytics dashboard are all included. There are no premium tiers, credits, trials or per-unlock fees. We do not charge visitors either.

### How does a visitor unlock my content?
The flow is the same for every link:
- The visitor opens your short link and sees the actions you configured.
- We create a private session that lasts two hours.
- The visitor completes each action in order and returns to the card.
- When every required step is complete, the content opens: a destination URL, a file download, or a message shown on the page.
The visitor never needs a Link Unlocker account unless the link asks for one.

### Which platforms and actions can I use?
The built-in catalog covers 22 platforms and 41 actions: YouTube, Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, X, Twitch, Discord, Telegram, GitHub, Reddit, Bluesky, Mastodon, Steam, Spotify, SoundCloud, LinkedIn, Snapchat, Threads, Kick, Pinterest, WhatsApp and any other website. Actions include subscribe, like, comment, watch, share, follow, repost, star a repository, join a server, a group or a channel, boost a server, upvote a post, listen to a track and visit a page. You can combine several actions on one link and ask for an email address as an extra step.

### Are the actions verified?
Only six social actions support authenticated checks, when the operator enables and configures their provider:
- YouTube likes and subscriptions use Google OAuth.
- GitHub follows and repository stars use GitHub OAuth.
- Telegram channel and group membership use a private bot check-in to identify the visitor’s account before checking membership.

We do not accept a typed username as proof that an account belongs to the visitor. GitHub stars are public, but authentication is needed here to prove whose account is being checked.

All other social actions in the 22-platform, 41-action catalog use one click and remain unverified, including YouTube comments and all Discord, Twitch, Steam, Bluesky and Mastodon actions. This reflects what this implementation supports, not whether a platform has public records.

The master switch is on by default, but without configured credentials no social action is authenticated. Unsupported, unconfigured or disabled checks use one click. A configured check does not fail open: an unavailable API, denied consent or an action not found leaves the step pending and the visitor can retry. The dashboard distinguishes opened steps, authenticated confirmations and attempted checks the API could not answer; an unanswered check is not a completion.

### What does the visitor have to share?
One-click social steps do not ask for an account connection. Configured YouTube and GitHub checks ask the visitor to authorize their own account through the provider. OAuth permissions may allow reading more data than one action, but this implementation reads only what the relevant check needs, never posts, follows or changes anything, and uses the visitor access token for the check without persisting it.

For Telegram, the visitor presses Start in a private chat with our bot. We store the Telegram account id, username if supplied, and membership result. No typed username is accepted as identity proof, and we never ask for a platform password. The optional email step stores an address after consent. A Link Unlocker account is not required just to authorize a social check.

### What happens if a link expires or is paused?
You can set an expiry date on any link. Once a link expires, or while it is paused, the unlock page stops immediately and tells the visitor that the link is no longer available. You can re-enable a paused link from your dashboard at any time. An expired session cannot be extended from the browser; the visitor starts again with a fresh session.

### Who can see the content I protect?
Only a visitor whose session completed every required step. The server checks the session on every request and refuses incomplete sessions, so a copied unlock URL on its own does not reveal anything. Downloads are issued per session. A destination URL is visible to the visitor once it is unlocked, so treat it as shareable and do not put secrets in a URL you hand out.

### Can I collect email addresses?
Yes, as an optional action. Visitors see why the address is requested and must actively consent before it is stored. Addresses are kept per link, visible only to you, and can be exported as a CSV file or deleted from the dashboard. We never sell them or share them with other creators.

### Do I need an account to use Link Unlocker?
You can publish one link as a guest; the browser keeps a signed cookie so you can still manage that link. A free account is required for additional links, file uploads, email lists, analytics, milestones and the bio page.

### Can I protect a file instead of a website link?
Yes. Upload a file from the dashboard, choose the file-download mode when you create the link, and the file is streamed only after the visitor completes the steps. Files are private by default and must match the type and size limits set by the operator of this installation.

### What analytics will I see?
You get counts of views, unlock starts, completed actions and completed unlocks for each link, a 14-day chart and a per-link conversion table. These are aggregate counts attached to the link, not profiles of individual visitors. We do not sell analytics or pass them to advertisers.

### How long does a link last?
A link stays available until you delete it, unless you set an expiry date. Each unlock session lasts two hours, which is usually enough to complete the steps without keeping a session open indefinitely.

### What is not allowed?
No malware, phishing, pirated content, harassment, impersonation, scams, or anything that breaks the rules of the platform you are using. Do not ask visitors for passwords, payment details or identity documents. Do not use the service to collect email addresses for spam. We can disable links and accounts that generate credible abuse reports.

### How do I report a link?
Use the report link shown on the unlock page, or send us the short link through the contact page. Reports are reviewed first and are not shown to the link owner. If you include an email address we can reply when the report is resolved.

### Can I delete my data?
Deleting a link also deletes its unlock sessions, analytics and collected email addresses. You can delete individual addresses from your email list at any time. To close your account and remove your profile data, contact us — there is no self-service delete button yet, so we handle it manually.

### What if a platform changes its API?
A configured check stays pending if the API cannot answer or consent is denied. It does not complete or receive a verified result; the visitor can retry after access or availability is restored. The operator can explicitly disable checking, which returns social steps to one-click, unverified behavior. Unsupported or unconfigured checks already use that behavior. The creator can update a changed destination from the dashboard.

### How do I get help?
Email [support@linkunlock.app](mailto:support@linkunlock.app) for product questions or account help, and use the report link on an unlock page for abuse. Including the short link and the step you are stuck on helps us answer faster.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: What we collect, why we collect it, and the controls you have — written in plain language, without the legal maze.
privacy.helpBody: Ask for a copy, a correction or a deletion, and we will help.
privacy.content:
## Who this policy covers
Link Unlocker is operated by the team behind this website ("we", "us"). This policy explains what happens to personal data when you browse the public site, unlock a link, create links as a creator or contact us. It applies to this installation of the service, not to the social platforms you interact with — those platforms have their own policies, and completing an action there is also governed by their rules.

## Data we collect
- **Account data:** your name, email address and a hashed password when you register, plus profile details such as an avatar if you add them.
- **Link and file data:** the links you create, their configuration, the destination URLs you paste, uploaded cover images and any files you protect.
- **Email leads:** addresses visitors submit to you through the optional email action, together with the time they consented.
- **Unlock and analytics data:** views, unlock starts, completed actions, completed unlocks, and technical data such as a hashed IP address, browser user-agent and referring page.
- **Account-check data:** platform check outcomes and evidence references; for Telegram, the account id, username if supplied, and membership result associated with the unlock step. Visitor OAuth access tokens are not persisted.
- **Abuse reports:** the link you report, the reason and details you provide, an optional email address, and a hashed IP address.
- **Support messages:** whatever you send us when you ask for help.
We do not ask for payment details because the service has no paid plans.

## How we use the data
We use account and link data to run, secure and support the service; analytics data to show creators how their links perform; email leads to deliver the addresses a visitor chose to share with that creator; and abuse reports to investigate misuse. Technical data is used for rate limiting, fraud prevention and keeping sessions working. We do not use your data to build advertising profiles about you.

## Legal bases
Where data protection law requires a legal basis, we rely on:
- **Contract:** to provide the service you asked for.
- **Legitimate interests:** to secure the service, prevent abuse and understand aggregate performance.
- **Consent:** for optional email collection, authorization of platform account checks where required, and any non-essential cookie that asks for it. Email consent is given to the creator; account access is authorized with the platform.
- **Legal obligation:** to respond to valid legal requests or to defend legal claims.

## Cookies and local storage
- **Session cookie:** keeps a signed-in creator signed in. It is HTTP-only and same-site.
- **Guest cookie:** remembers the one free link created by a guest so the same browser can still manage it.
- **Locale cookie:** remembers the language you chose.
- **Theme preference:** may be stored in your browser so light or dark mode survives a reload.
These are used to make the service work. If the operator enables an advertising unit, that ad may load resources from its own provider and may set its own cookies; we do not pass your account details or collected email addresses to advertisers.

## Unlock sessions and visitor data
When a visitor opens a link, we create a short-lived session that expires after two hours. For unlock analytics and rate limiting we store the visitor's IP address only as a salted hash, together with the browser user-agent and referring page. Sign-in sessions may also record an IP address and browser so an account holder can review access. We use this data to keep the service available and to investigate abuse, not to follow visitors around the web.

## Email addresses collected by creators
The email action is optional and only appears when a creator adds it to a link. The address is stored with the time of consent, only the owner of that link can see or export it, and it is deleted when the link is deleted or when the owner removes it. Creators are responsible for using those addresses lawfully and for honouring any withdrawal of consent they receive.

## Completed steps and platform checks
One-click social steps record completion when opened, without confirming the platform action. For configured account checks, opening is recorded but completion requires the platform to confirm the action on the authenticated visitor account. We store check outcomes and evidence references for the step and session. An unanswered API attempt may also leave an unverified record; that record does not complete the step. Evidence can contain account identifiers and target references, so it is not anonymous data.

Google OAuth checks YouTube likes and subscriptions; GitHub OAuth checks follows and repository stars. We authenticate the visitor’s account rather than accepting a typed username as proof of ownership. GitHub stars are public; authentication ties that public action to the visitor. OAuth scopes may permit reading more data, but this implementation reads only what the relevant action check needs. It never posts, follows or changes the account and does not persist the visitor access token. We never ask for a platform password.

Telegram uses a private bot check-in: pressing Start identifies the visitor’s account, then the bot queries membership of the target channel or group. We store the check-in’s Telegram account id, username if Telegram supplies one, and membership result, linked to the unlock session and step.

Other social actions, including YouTube comments, Discord, Twitch, Steam, Bluesky and Mastodon, use one click without authentication or verification. The master switch defaults on, but credentials must be configured for a social check to authenticate anyone. Unsupported, unconfigured or disabled checks use one click. If a configured check cannot answer, consent is denied or the action is not found, the step stays pending and can be retried; inability to check is never a verified result.

## Files and uploads
Files and images you upload are stored by the service and delivered only to sessions that completed the link's steps. File names, sizes and MIME types are stored so the file can be streamed and shown in the dashboard. Deleting a file disables the links that referenced it.

## Sharing and processors
We do not sell personal data. We share the minimum necessary with:
- Google, GitHub or Telegram when you authorize a configured account check or use the Telegram bot; requests include the information needed to identify the account and check the target action.
- Hosting and database providers that run the service.
- Email delivery providers, when a password-reset or contact email has to be sent.
- Authorities or other parties when the law requires it, or when it is necessary to investigate credible abuse.
These providers process data on our instructions or under their own terms, and may operate in countries other than yours. Where required, we rely on appropriate safeguards for those transfers.

## Retention
Unlock sessions expire after two hours. Analytics events are kept while the link exists so a creator can see historical totals. Email leads are kept until the link or the individual address is deleted. Abuse reports are kept as long as needed to resolve the report and prevent repeat abuse. Rate-limit records are short-lived. Deleting a link removes its sessions, events and leads with it. Backup copies may remain for a short period before they are overwritten.

## Security
Passwords are hashed, traffic is served over HTTPS, session cookies are HTTP-only, and access to another creator's links is checked on the server. We apply rate limits to sensitive actions. No service can promise perfect security, but we keep the surface small: we do not store payment details.

## Your rights
Depending on where you live, you may have the right to access, correct, export, restrict or delete your personal data, to object to some processing, and to withdraw consent. You can exercise most of these from the dashboard. For anything else, contact us and we will respond within the time required by law. You also have the right to complain to your local data-protection authority.

## Children
The service is not intended for children below the age at which they can consent to data processing in their country. We do not knowingly collect data from children. If you believe a child has created an account, contact us and we will remove it.

## Changes to this policy
We update this page when the way we handle data changes. The date at the top shows when it was last reviewed. If a change is material, we will announce it on the site or by email to account holders.

## Contact
Questions, requests or complaints: [support@linkunlock.app](mailto:support@linkunlock.app). We answer privacy requests first.

terms.title: Terms of service
terms.intro: The rules for using Link Unlocker as a creator, a visitor or a reporter, in plain language.
terms.helpBody: Ask before you rely on a clause — we would rather explain than surprise you.
terms.content:
## Agreement to these terms
By using Link Unlocker — as a creator, a visitor or a reporter — you agree to these terms. If you do not agree, do not use the service. If you use the service for an organisation, you confirm that you are allowed to accept these terms for it.

## What the service does
Link Unlocker lets a creator publish a short link whose content is revealed after a visitor completes configured actions, such as following a channel or joining a server. The service is free and has no paid plans. We do not charge visitors and do not pay creators; there is no reward, sweepstake or prize connected to the service.

## Accounts and guest links
You can create one link as a guest. Additional links and features such as files, email lists, analytics and the bio page require a free account. Keep your credentials secure and tell us promptly if you believe someone else has access to your account. You are responsible for activity under your account.

## Your responsibilities as a creator
You must:
- own or have permission to share the content you protect;
- describe the protected content honestly and deliver what the page promises;
- ask only for actions you are entitled to request, and respect each platform's rules;
- collect email addresses only with clear consent and use them lawfully;
- keep your links and their destinations up to date, and remove content you no longer have the right to share.
You are the controller of the email addresses you collect through your links. Link Unlocker stores and displays them to you but does not use them for its own marketing.

## Prohibited uses
Do not use Link Unlocker to:
- distribute malware, phishing pages, pirated material or content that infringes someone else's rights;
- harass, threaten, impersonate or deceive people;
- run scams, fake giveaways or engagement schemes that break a platform's rules;
- ask visitors for passwords, payment card details, government identifiers or other sensitive credentials;
- collect email addresses for spam, resale or unrelated marketing;
- probe, overload or attempt to bypass the service's security or rate limits.
We may remove content or disable links and accounts that breach these rules.

## Third-party platforms
Actions take place on third-party platforms whose availability, rules and data practices we do not control. When enabled and configured, Google OAuth checks YouTube likes and subscriptions, GitHub OAuth checks follows and stars, and a private Telegram bot check-in identifies the visitor before checking channel or group membership. A typed username is not proof of account ownership. The implementation only reads what the relevant check needs, never posts or changes the account, and does not persist visitor access tokens, even if OAuth permissions allow broader reading.

Other social actions, including YouTube comments, Discord, Twitch, Steam, Bluesky and Mastodon, are one-click and unverified. Unsupported, unconfigured or disabled checks also use one click. Configured checks stay pending if the provider cannot answer, consent is denied or the action is not found; visitors can retry. We do not label an unavailable result as verified. Creators can update removed or changed destinations.

## Content and ownership
You keep the rights you already hold in the content you upload or link to. You give us a limited licence to store, display and deliver that content for the purpose of running your links and showing them in your dashboard. You confirm that you have the rights needed to grant that licence. We own the service, its software and its branding; these terms do not transfer any of that ownership to you.

## Visitors and consent
Visitors must complete the steps themselves. Creators must not complete actions on a visitor's behalf, automate them, or misrepresent what will be unlocked. Email collection requires an affirmative consent from the visitor; pre-ticked boxes, bundled consent or a requirement hidden in unrelated copy do not count. Creators must honour withdrawal of consent and applicable marketing law in the visitor's country.

## Files and limits
Uploaded files must match the allowed types and size limits shown in the dashboard, which the operator can change. Do not use file delivery to distribute material you do not have the right to share. We may disable a file and any links that depend on it if it breaches these terms or generates an abuse report.

## Availability and changes
The service is provided on an as-is and as-available basis. We may add, change or discontinue features, set usage limits, or suspend the service for maintenance. Where a change materially affects your links, we will try to give reasonable notice on the site or by email. We do not guarantee that a link will stay online forever.

## Suspension and termination
You can stop using the service at any time and delete your links. We may suspend or terminate access if you breach these terms, if your links generate credible abuse reports, or if the law requires it. Where practical, we will explain the reason. Content that is illegal, harmful or the subject of a valid complaint may be removed immediately.

## Disclaimers
We do not promise a particular number of followers, views, clicks, unlocks or revenue. An authenticated confirmation reflects only the supported action and the platform’s answer at the time of the check, not future engagement or continued membership. One-click completion is not proof of a social action. A configured check that cannot answer remains pending, not completed or verified. We do not guarantee the availability or accuracy of third-party APIs. The service is provided without warranties to the extent permitted by law. Nothing in these terms excludes mandatory consumer rights.

## Limitation of liability
To the extent permitted by law, we are not liable for indirect or consequential loss, loss of profit, loss of data, or loss caused by a third-party platform, a visitor's conduct or content you chose to protect. Where liability cannot be excluded, it is limited to the amount you paid us in the twelve months before the claim — which, because the service is free, is zero. This does not limit liability for fraud, wilful misconduct or anything else that cannot be limited by law.

## Indemnity
You agree to indemnify us against claims and costs arising from content you protected, actions you asked visitors to complete, or your breach of these terms or of a third party's rights, to the extent permitted by law. We will tell you about a claim and let you take part in the defence.

## Governing law and disputes
These terms are governed by the laws that apply to the operator of this site, without regard to conflict-of-law rules. If you are a consumer, you keep the protection of the mandatory laws of your country of residence and may bring a claim there. Before starting a formal dispute, contact us so we can try to resolve it.

## Changes to these terms
We may update these terms as the service evolves. The date at the top shows the current version. If a change is material, we will announce it on the site or by email to account holders. Continuing to use the service after the change means you accept the updated terms.

## Contact
Questions about these terms: [support@linkunlock.app](mailto:support@linkunlock.app). For a link that breaks these rules, use the report link on its unlock page.

story.metaDescription: Why Link Unlocker exists: one honest step between a visitor and the content a creator shared.
story.title: Built because unlock pages were getting in the way
story.intro: Most unlock tools ask for add-ons, puzzles or an account before anything opens. We wanted the opposite: one fair step that supports the creator and opens the door.

sections.title: The problem we kept seeing
sections.body: A link gets shared, the content matters, and the only way to open it asks for five unrelated steps. Visitors give up, creators lose trust and everyone learns to distrust the word unlock.

sections.title: A shorter path
sections.body: Link Unlocker keeps the reward and drops the maze. Every step is a real, named social action: subscribe to that channel, follow that account, join that server. The visitor presses once and the page remembers it.

sections.title: Where we are today
sections.body: Creators use unlock pages for files, downloads, offers and early access. Everything around them follows one rule: the page has to be fair to the person clicking.

what.metaDescription: Unlock pages, short links, bio pages, analytics and ad placements from one platform.
what.title: Simple tools that connect creators and visitors
what.intro: Everything starts with one link. Around it we build the pieces that make sharing, unlocking and measuring feel effortless.

sections.title: Unlock pages
sections.body: Choose a URL, a piece of text or a file, then ask for the social actions you actually want. Steps use the real names of your channels, so visitors know exactly what they are supporting.

sections.title: Short links and bio pages
sections.body: Compact links for bios and messages, plus bio pages that hold every link you share. Both keep their own analytics.

sections.title: Analytics and reach
sections.body: Views, unlocks and completions per link and per day, email leads when you ask for an address, and optional ad placements when you want to earn from traffic.

values.metaDescription: Visitor first, clear rules and no dark patterns: the principles behind every Link Unlocker page.
values.title: Fair by default
values.intro: Unlock pages only work while people trust them. These are the rules we hold ourselves to, even when a shortcut would convert better.

sections.title: The visitor comes first
sections.body: A step is recorded the moment it is pressed, progress is saved, and no account is required to unlock anything. No fake countdowns and no extra hoops.

sections.title: Clear rules, visible terms
sections.body: Only real social actions from the platform catalog, a public report button on every link, and terms anyone can read before sharing.

sections.title: Privacy with a purpose
sections.body: We collect what a link needs to work, aggregate the rest, and let the site owner shorten how long analytics are kept.

howItWorks.metaDescription: Create an unlock page, share the link and let visitors open it with one click.
howItWorks.title: One page, one click, unlocked
howItWorks.intro: An unlock page is a single link with a short list of social actions. A visitor completes one, the reward opens, and every completion lands in your dashboard.

create.body: Pick what sits behind the page and the actions you ask for in return.

share.body: Post the link in a bio, a message or a story. No install for visitors.

unlock.title: Unlock a reward
unlock.body: One click opens the step and marks it done, then the content appears.

create.metaDescription: Choose the reward, add social actions and publish an unlock link.
create.title: Create your unlock page
create.intro: Start with what you are unlocking, then add the steps you want in return. The whole page takes a few minutes.

sections.title: Pick the reward
sections.body: A destination URL, a block of text or a file you upload. The page shows a clear title, an optional cover and the steps that guard it.

sections.title: Add the steps
sections.body: Choose from the platform catalog — subscribe on YouTube, follow on Instagram or TikTok, join a Discord server, listen on Spotify, visit a website — and set their order.

sections.title: Publish and copy the link
sections.body: Publish once and the link is live. Guests can create one for free from the same flow, and you can disable or expire a link at any time.

share.metaDescription: Where an unlock link works, how short links and bio pages fit, and how to keep control of it.
share.title: Share it anywhere your audience already is
share.intro: An unlock link is a normal URL, so it fits wherever you post: bios, descriptions, messages, stories and comments.

sections.title: Every channel
sections.body: Paste the link directly, or shorten it first to keep bios tidy and count clicks. Bio pages collect all of your links on one address.

sections.title: Guests can create too
sections.body: People without an account can build a link and share it from the create page. The link belongs to a browser session, so it is managed from the same device.

sections.title: Keep control
sections.body: Every link can be disabled, given an expiry date or reported by a visitor. Reports go to the site team and abusive links are removed.

unlock.metaDescription: What a visitor sees on an unlock page, why steps are named, and when the reward opens.
unlock.title: What the visitor's one click does
unlock.intro: The unlock card lists each step with the real channel or page name, so nobody has to guess what a button will do.

sections.title: Named steps, no jargon
sections.body: A row reads “Subscribe to” with the channel name, or “Follow” with the account name. It opens in a new tab and leaves the unlock page where it was, so a step never hides its destination.

sections.title: Completion that is remembered
sections.body: Pressing a step records it immediately, and the page can show a short settling wait before the row reads as done. Refreshing never loses progress.

sections.title: What the visitor gets
sections.body: When every step is complete the reward — a link, a text or a file — opens on the same page. If the owner asks for an email address, it is requested once and never blocks the content.

backups.title: Backups
backups.description: Snapshot the database and uploaded files, and restore a snapshot when something goes wrong.
backups.unavailableTitle: Backups are managed by this host
backups.unavailableManaged: This deployment runs on a managed platform with an ephemeral filesystem, so the app cannot take or restore backups here. Use the database provider's backup tooling, or run the app on a server with persistent storage.
backups.unavailableDisabled: System operations have been disabled by the SYSTEM_OPS_DISABLED environment variable.
backups.unavailableEnvironment: The backup folder is not writable, or the required tools (mysqldump, mysql, tar) are missing on this host.

create.title: Create a backup
create.description: Each backup runs in the background and keeps working if you leave this page.

backups.panelDescription: Newest first. Restoring overwrites live data, so a safety backup is taken first.
backups.restoreDescription: This replaces live data with the snapshot. A full safety backup is taken before anything is changed.
backups.restoreWarning: Visitors may see errors while the restore runs. Restoring the database does not remove newer migrations; take a copy of any data you need to keep.
backups.deleteDescription: The archive is removed from disk and cannot be recovered.
backups.deleteFailed: The backup could not be deleted. Try again, or check the server logs.

updates.title: System updates
updates.description: Check the configured branch for new commits, review the changes, and install them with a safety backup and automatic rollback.
updates.unavailableTitle: Updates are managed by this host
updates.unavailableManaged: This deployment builds from Git on a managed platform. Deploy a new commit through the platform instead; the app cannot rebuild itself here.
updates.unavailableDisabled: System operations have been disabled by the SYSTEM_OPS_DISABLED environment variable.
updates.unavailableEnvironment: This installation is not a Git checkout, or Git/npm are unavailable on this host.
updates.currentDescription: The commit currently serving this site.
updates.restartNote: No process manager is configured, so an update will build the new code but you must restart the service yourself to activate it. Set this under Settings → System operations.
updates.processManagerNote: Updates restart {name} through {manager} and verify /api/health afterwards.
updates.checkDescription: Fetches the configured branch and lists commits that are not installed yet.
updates.upToDate: Everything on this branch is installed.
updates.aheadNote: This checkout is {count} commits ahead of the remote branch.
updates.installDescription: The server will fetch the branch, install dependencies, apply migrations, build and restart.
updates.installWarning: The site may be unavailable for a few minutes. A full safety backup is taken first, and the code is rolled back automatically if the build or health check fails.
updates.safetyBackupNote: A full backup is taken automatically before installing.
updates.dirtyBlocked: Commit or stash local changes before updating; the installer refuses to touch a dirty working tree.
updates.rollbackDescription: The code returns to the commit that was running before this update. Data is not rolled back.
updates.rollbackWarning: A safety backup is taken first. Migrations applied by the newer version are not undone.
updates.historyDescription: Every install attempt and rollback, newest first. Archive entries you no longer need.
updates.historyEmpty: No updates have been installed from this console yet.
updates.historyEmptyArchived: No updates have been archived yet.
updates.deleteDescription: The entry is removed from the update history. The code and data on the server are not touched.
